leading_positions.synthesis: Three members include base editing (B060) in their round-1 configuration, always as David Liu alone, and always as one part of a two-part prize: Brzezinski pairs it with B030 (Gray and Winkler), Chabes with B041 (Crews and Deshaies), Somfai with B023 (Buchwald and Hartwig). What is shared is Liu as the decisive originator and the single-name credit that keeps the total within three laureates. What is not shared is the partner achievement, and therefore the prize's overall theme. Reservations stated by supporters are proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize, short clinical record, whether it is chemistry or biology, and whether Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida should share credit. Aili, Aqvist and I list B060 only as an alternative.

Two members include targeted protein degradation (B041) in their configuration, both naming Crews and Deshaies. They differ on the third name and on scope: Aili adds Ciulli and frames the citation around heterobifunctional small molecules recruiting E3 ligases, while Chabes stops at two names and frames it as chemically induced proximity, leaving open the cereblon and molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray). Both note that no PROTAC is yet approved. Aili stands for B041 alone, Chabes pairs it with B060.

Two members include Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B023) with Buchwald and Hartwig as the decisive pair, citing a general, mature, widely used method with clean two-person attribution. Both acknowledge Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling as a real precursor but not the general catalytic method, and both flag overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Aqvist proposes B023 alone; Somfai pairs it with B060.

I am the only member to include nanopore sequencing (B039), with Deamer, Akeson and Bayley. Support is confined to my own configuration, and Aili, Chabes and Sparr, who ranked it in the opening, did not carry it into round 1. Several members describe it as physically clear and commercially validated, but credit is spread over at least five people and the chemistry-versus-instrumentation question is open.

Only Sparr includes biomolecular phase separation (B052), with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. Others who commented (Aili, Chabes, Aqvist, Linke) accept the conceptual reach but question the strength of the in vivo evidence, the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag, and whether it is chemistry.

Only Brzezinski includes long-range protein electron transfer (B030), with Gray and Winkler, as one part of a two-part prize with B060. Brzezinski states that no other member ranked it in the opening and does not oppose B023 as a stronger-supported alternative.

Only Zou includes halide perovskite solar absorbers (B010), with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith. Stability, lead toxicity and a six-way credit contest (Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also named) are the stated reservations.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has majority support: the eight round-1 configurations are spread over seven shortlisted ballots (B010, B023, B030, B039, B041, B052, B060), the largest explicit backing is three members for B060, and five votes are needed.
All eight configurations name at most three laureates in total, so the three-laureate limit is a shared working constraint.

B060 has the broadest cross-field presence: three members include it in their configuration and three more (Aili, Aqvist, Zou) list it as an alternative, with David Liu named as the decisive originator in every statement that discusses it.
Members agree that B023 has the cleanest attribution (Buchwald and Hartwig) and the longest record, and that its main weakness is proximity to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Several members report unresolved attribution or maturity questions on their own first choice, so no configuration is presented as free of risk.
scientific_disputes: Whether B060 is a distinct chemical discovery (deaminase chemistry made programmable) or a downstream extension of the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether it is chemistry or biology (Somfai, Chabes, Brzezinski).
Whether B023 is a substantive new method or an incremental extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize (Aqvist, Somfai, Zou, Brzezinski).

Whether B052 rests on settled physical chemistry or on a label applied beyond quantitative phase-diagram evidence, given disagreement over which cellular condensates are truly phase separated (Sparr, Aili, Chabes, Aqvist, Linke).
Whether B039 is chemistry or analytical-physical instrumentation, and whether the commercial instrument reflects the original discovery or later engineering (Linke, Chabes).
Whether B030 adds enough beyond Marcus theory (1992) to justify a prize now, or is mature and incremental (Brzezinski).
attribution_disputes: B041: whether the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) form one achievement or two. Aili names Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli; Chabes names Crews and Deshaies only; my own opening ballot used Crews, Ciulli and Handa; Brzezinski's opening ballot used Handa in place of Ciulli. The configurations differ in citation framing as well as in names.

B060: Liu alone (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Somfai, Zou in the opening proposals) against adding Komor and Gaudelli (Sparr's opening proposal) and the independent Kondo and Nishida Target-AID work (raised by Brzezinski, Chabes and Somfai).
B023: Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling versus the general catalytic systems of Buchwald and Hartwig (Aqvist, Somfai).

B039: a three-person cut among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson necessarily omits Branton or Kasianowicz, whose 1996 translocation experiment is the founding result; the committee has not agreed which three.
B052: the three-person limit excludes Pappu and Mittag, who supplied the sequence grammar and physical theory (Sparr, Aqvist).
B010: Miyasaka, Park and Snaith against Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis (Zou).
maturity_disputes: B041: no PROTAC is approved, so recognition may be a few years early (Aili, Chabes); I described its maturity as partly forward looking.
B060: clinical record is short and long-term safety is unproven (Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai).
B052: more than a decade of work, but the in vivo controversy is unresolved and some members see it as premature for Chemistry (Sparr, Aili).
B010: efficiencies above 25 percent and wide replication, but operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved (Zou).
B030 and B023 are described as fully mature, with the question being timeliness and novelty rather than readiness; B039 is described by its supporter as commercially validated for over a decade.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member discloses a personal, institutional, mentor or collaborator tie to any credited name on the shortlist; all eight conflict notes say no specific conflict is apparent.

Linke (chair): own research on molecular motors and Brownian ratchets is conceptually adjacent to the enzyme-ratchet step in B039, and the chair is the sole supporter of B039; the chair has stated he should avoid steering discussion.
Brzezinski: own research on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is adjacent to B030, which he alone supports; no tie to Gray or Winkler.
Somfai: Pd-catalysed coupling is close to his own field of synthetic methodology, disclosed as a disciplinary bias rather than a personal tie to B023.
Sparr: lipid and membrane physical chemistry is close to B066 and B052, and she shares a Lund tradition with Linke and Somfai; no stated tie to any candidate.
Aili: shares peptide and protein self-assembly interests with Sparr, relevant to B052 only as field overlap; Chabes: dNTP pools and replication fidelity are thematically adjacent to B060 and B039.
Zou and Brzezinski are Stockholm University colleagues; neither has a nominee in the other's configuration.
questions_for_round2: B060: is base editing a distinct chemical discovery rather than an extension of the 2020 CRISPR prize, and if it is recognised, is Liu alone the right credit or should Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo or Nishida be added?

B060 pairing: Brzezinski, Chabes and Somfai each pair B060 with a different second achievement (B030, B041, B023). Which second part, if any, can a majority of five support, and does any two-part pairing hold a coherent citation?

B041: should the citation cover PROTACs only (Crews, Deshaies, with or without Ciulli) or include the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa and others), and which three names would a majority accept given that no PROTAC is yet approved?
B023: is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize disqualifying or only a mild concern, and how much weight should Kosugi's 1983 precedent carry against Buchwald and Hartwig?
B039: can the committee agree which three of Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson to credit, and does it regard nanopore sensing as chemistry rather than analytical physics?
B052: can the founding in vitro and P-granule demonstrations stand independently of the in vivo controversy, and is leaving out Pappu and Mittag acceptable?
For members whose first choice has single-member support (B010, B030, B039, B052): which, if any, would move to a second-choice configuration, and what would it need to see to do so?
summary.chair_observation: After round 1 no ballot reaches the five votes needed. B060 has the most explicit backing (three members) but always paired with a different partner or with no agreed partner; B041 and B023 each have two supporters; B010, B030, B039 and B052 each have one. Debate has centred on distinguishing recent chemical-biology candidates from the 2020 CRISPR and 2010 cross-coupling prizes, and on unresolved credit among several candidates. This summary records positions only and does not favour any configuration, including my own.
